headline: VISIBLE GOLD IN 52 HOLES: GOLIATH SUREBET BONANZA ZONE GROWS 19% TO 1.51 KM², BEST INTERVAL 9.12 G/T AuEq
snippet: Goliath Resources (TSXV: GOT) released September 18 assay results from three new Bonanza Zone holes at the Surebet Discovery in BC's Golden Triangle — hole GD-26-431 returned 9.12 g/t AuEq over 11.27 metres including 74.66 g/t AuEq over 1.03 metres with visible gold to the naked eye, while GD-26-442 cut 31.42 g/t AuEq over 1.0 metre; the Bonanza Zone has grown 19% to 1.51 km² and the full Surebet system footprint increased 12% to 2.01 km², with visible gold logged in 52 of 92 holes drilled in the fully funded 50,000-metre 2026 program. The system remains open laterally and at depth.

headline: COPPER RALLIES THIRD STRAIGHT SESSION ON CHINESE SEABORNE SURGE 43% — FREEPORT +2.3%, SOUTHERN COPPER +3.3%
snippet: Copper posted three consecutive sessions of gains on September 18 as Chinese physical buyers returned to the seaborne market ahead of the October 1–7 National Day holiday, with daily transaction volumes jumping 43% to 1.41 million tonnes; LME copper moved toward $14,200/t while Southern Copper rose 3.28% to US$196.11 and Freeport-McMoRan gained 2.33% to US$70.85 — the rally now hinges on whether Chinese restocking demand persists past the holiday break or proves a one-time pre-holiday pull-forward.

headline: GOLD HOLDS $4,384 AS BoJ JOINS FED IN HIKING — ASIAN BUYERS ABSORB TWIN CENTRAL BANK TIGHTENING
snippet: Gold advanced to $4,384.78 on September 18, up 1.00% on the day, as Asian metals markets absorbed the Bank of Japan's September 17–18 rate decision — its own hiking cycle proceeding in parallel with the Fed's first hike since 2023 — without triggering significant selling; GoldSeek's daily Asian metals update notes more bullish than bearish factors for gold and silver over six-month-plus horizons, with central bank demand continuing uninterrupted and physical demand for copper, silver and non-ferrous metals running near available supply or in deficit.

headline: SILVER SOLAR DEMAND DESTRUCTION: MANUFACTURERS CUT USE 19% ON HIGH PRICES — 40M OZ ANNUAL DEFICIT HOLDS
snippet: Analysis published September 17 reveals a structural tension in the silver market: solar photovoltaic manufacturers have cut silver use by 19% at current elevated prices as demand destruction kicks in at the margin, and jewellery and silverware demand is contracting double-digits in price-sensitive markets like India; yet coin and bar investment demand is forecast to rise 18% in 2026 following a 14% jump in 2025, keeping the market in a structural deficit of 40.3 million ounces and reinforcing the silver bull case even as industrial consumption thins at the margin.

headline: PUREPOINT HITS 8,760 CPS AT UNCONFORMITY IN FIRST HOLE AT NEW Q24 TARGET — ATHABASCA BASIN DORADO JV
snippet: Purepoint Uranium (TSXV: PTU) reported September 17 that the first drill hole at the new Q24 target within its Dorado Joint Venture with IsoEnergy in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin intersected 7.4 metres averaging 8,760 counts per second (cps) at the unconformity, including 0.5 metres averaging 38,710 cps in strongly altered and structurally disrupted graphitic basement rocks — the same geological signature that characterises high-grade uranium deposits in the basin; Q24 is a separate target from both the Nova Discovery and Q23, and laboratory assays are pending.

headline: ANSON CLEARS UTAH ENVIRONMENTAL HURDLE — YELLOW CAT URANIUM-VANADIUM PHASE 2 JORC DRILLING NOW APPROVED
snippet: Anson Resources (ASX: ASN) confirmed September 18 that an extensive environmental baseline field survey across the western and central blocks of its Yellow Cat Uranium-Vanadium Project in Utah returned no environmental obstacles, paving the way for Notice of Intent to Drill submissions to the Bureau of Land Management and Utah DOGM; Phase 2 drilling will twin three to five historical holes to upgrade legacy resource estimates to 2012 JORC standards, with assay results expected progressively in early 2027 — a key step in building a compliant resource estimate at a US uranium project.

headline: IRON ORE BACK ABOVE $106 ON CHINESE HOLIDAY STOCKPILING — GOLDMAN SACHS WARNS OCTOBER-NOVEMBER DEMAND SOFTENS
snippet: Iron ore futures rose to 711 CNY/t (~US$105.94) on September 18 as Chinese steelmakers booked seaborne cargoes ahead of the October 1–7 National Day holiday, with Vale climbing 2.41%; however Goldman Sachs analysts warn that Chinese steel production and iron ore demand will soften materially in October–November as low-cost seaborne supply from major producers and the new Simandou project in Guinea increases — a cautionary signal for base metals broadly at a time when pre-holiday buying is masking structural demand weakness.

headline: PELANGIO ADVANCES THREE GHANA GOLD PROGRAMS, FLAGS 14 G/T Au HISTORICAL TARGET AT DANKRAN
snippet: Pelangio Exploration (TSXV: PX) announced September 18 that three exploration programs across its Ghana portfolio are now running in parallel: a 5-hole, 650-metre diamond program at Dankran following up historical intercepts including 3 metres at 14.17 g/t Au and 2 metres at 6.02 g/t Au; extensions to the high-grade Pokukrom East gold shoot at Manfo, where 2026 drilling extended the zone 150 metres north at 26 metres of 2.99 g/t Au; and initial results from the Kotoso target — with the company treating all three programs as having individual resource-scale potential.

headline: 20+ JUNIOR MINERS HEAD TO LONDON FOR GENTILE'S INAUGURAL FORUM — FIRST EUROPEAN INSTITUTIONAL ROADSHOW OF THE CYCLE
snippet: More than 20 junior mining companies confirmed September 18 participation in the inaugural Gentile Mining Investor Forum in London's Mayfair on October 19, followed by a five-city European roadshow through Paris, Frankfurt, Zurich and Munich from October 20–23; companies including Group Eleven Resources, Maple Gold, Radisson Mining, Valkea Resources, Leviathan Metals, Astra Exploration and ONGold Resources will meet an expected 150 institutional and high-net-worth investors — sponsored by ATB Cormark, Beacon Securities and Stifel — marking the first coordinated European capital-raising push for Gentile-affiliated juniors since the current bull market began.

headline: GOLD MINER VALUATIONS STILL LAGGING $4,400 SPOT — ANALYSTS ARGUE SHARE PRICES HAVEN'T CAUGHT UP WITH SUSTAINED HIGH GOLD
snippet: A September 2026 analyst roundup argues that despite GDX posting a 54% trailing one-year return, gold mining equity valuations remain below the levels that prevailed before 2025's major rally — meaning that at $4,400 gold today's share prices still embed below-spot gold price assumptions, creating operating-leverage upside if prices hold or continue rising; the piece highlights Agnico Eagle's low-risk Canadian asset base, Newmont's 5.3 million ounce 2026 production guidance, and the structural gap between record gold earnings and the multiples the market is willing to assign them.
